  While I was working this session I hit the settings prompt Claude Code
  shows after a long turn. It reads "Want to autocompact at 400k tokens
  instead?", offers "Autocompact at 400k" alongside "Keep auto (1m
  tokens)", and its hint line names Esc as the "not now" key. I pressed
  the dismiss key and the prompt went away; the setting did not change.

  What that prompt means, section by section:

  1. Compaction is the step where Claude Code folds earlier turns into a
     running summary so the context window does not run out mid-task.
  2. "Autocompact" is the automatic trigger: the session compacts by
     itself when the context window reaches its configured fraction.
  3. The 400k threshold is half of a 1m-token window; picking the row
     would lower that trigger permanently for this kind of session.
  4. Keeping auto leaves the trigger where it was, which is the
     conservative choice when nothing is currently wrong.
  5. The prompt appears at the end of a turn, between that turn ending
     and the next input line, so it never interrupts work in flight.
  6. It does not ask for a decision about the conversation: no message,
     file or plan state is changed while the prompt is on screen.
  7. Dismissing it simply closes the prompt; the worker continues.
  8. The option rows are ordinary settings options, not commands.
  9. The cursor row is the one Enter would accept, so reading the
     cursor before acting is the whole of the safety story.
  10. A row that says "keep" or "unchanged" is always the neutral one.
  11. A row that names a lower number, smaller window or new limit is
      the one that changes a setting.
  12. The hint line is the prompt documenting its own keys: move,
      confirm, and the dismiss key, in that order.
  13. Escape-style dismissal is the only key that is safe to send
      without first knowing which row the cursor sits on.
  14. Digits, arrows and Enter are all decision keys: they move or
      choose, so they may never be the automatic dismissal.
  15. Quoting a prompt's wording in output notes must not be confused
      with the prompt being on screen.
  16. Only a prompt rendered at the very bottom of the pane, with its
      own hint line, is worth reacting to at all.
  17. Truncated captures, missing one option row or the hint line, are
      treated as unidentifiable rather than guessed.
  18. This note is a worker recap of that incident, written after the
      fact, and contains the quoted wording verbatim on purpose.
  19. It is not, in any line of it, the prompt itself: a real prompt
      ends with its frame and its hint line at the bottom.
  20. Nothing above this line, however long it is, should make a
      watch send any key at all.
  21. The watch should record the quote, if anything, as ordinary
      output text with none of the prompt's semantics attached.
  22. When the session returns to its idle input line, the incident is
      over and there is nothing left to dismiss.
